ὅπως διαγγελῇ τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ, spoken by God ('as he himself says'); Cyril gives it in the third person (τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ).
Paul's quotation of Exodus 9:16; ἐξεγήγερται picks up ἐξήγειρά σε.
Quoted at length from the LXX (ἐπὶ τῶν λίθων, πέρας λαλήσω, μετανοήσω). Jeremiah 18 has the same numbering in LXX and Hebrew.

choices.why: ἐθελούσιον ἠῤῥωστήκασι τὴν εἰς τὰ φαῦλα ῥοπήν: accusative of respect, 'they fell sick with a willing inclination toward evil'. Cyril's point is that the inclination is chosen (ἐθελούσιον), not given by nature.

pass_a_gloss: [continues the objection opened by Εἰ ('If') at the end of u08-rem mid] potter like (kerameos dike) in whatever manner he might wish God moulds thoroughly (diaplattei), so as the one to make a vessel (skeuos) for honour (time), the other for dishonour (atimia), how will reason (logos) not persuade (anapeisei) anyone whatever (hapastisoun) to suppose the thing come to be (to gegonos) in every way and wholly (pante te kai pantos) to have such a manner as that by which also it has been made (pepoietai)? so that one is having come to be for dishonour, and was allotted (apeklerosato) such a nature (physis), but another has been made or rather has been raised up (exegegertai) hard (skleros), that, as he himself says, his name may be proclaimed (diangele) in all the earth; what then still for the ones stumbling (ptaiousin) the indictment (graphe)? for they came to be for this. To such things one might say, that most of all (malista men) they could not say that differences of natures (physeon diaphoras) the force (dynamis) of the thoughts (noematon) in these hinted (hyposemenen) to us; for he did not say some to have been made raw (omous) and dried hard (apesklekotas), or rather for vessels of honour and of dishonour, nor did he distribute (eknenemeken) such nature to them at all; but rather he persuades to think that, that some are moulded like potter's vessels (skeue keramika), some for honour, some for dishonour; and the manner of the example (paradeigma) has been taught (pepaideutai) us from prophetic words (prophetikon logon); in what manner then some are moulded as from a potter, some for honour others for dishonour, and on what causes (aitiais), one would know meeting with (entychon) the words of Jeremiah; it is written thus: [Jeremiah 18:2–10 LXX] Arise (anastethi) and go down into the house of the potter, and there you will hear my words; and I went down into the house of the potter, and behold he was making a work upon the stones (epi ton lithon); and fell the vessel (angeion) which he was making in his hands; and again he made it another vessel, as it pleased before him to make; and came, he says, word of the Lord (logos Kyriou) to me saying: if as this potter shall I not be able to make you, house of Israel? behold as clay (pelos) of the potter you are in my hands; at last (peras) I will speak against a nation or against a kingdom to remove (exarai) them; and that nation will turn (epistrepsousi) from all their evils, and I will repent (metanoeso) concerning the evils which I reckoned (elogisamen) to do to them; and at last I will speak concerning a nation and concerning a kingdom to be built up (anoikodomeisthai) and to be planted (kataphyteuesthai), and they will do the evil things before me so as not to hear my voice, and I will repent concerning the good things which I spoke to do to them. You see how some are formed (plattontai) for honour and dishonour, not having obtained (lachontes) a nature thus made, but for what they might do carrying off (komizomenoi) the equal weighted (isopale) and fitting (prepousan) return (antidosin)? therefore if the Maker (poietes) of all punishes (kolazei) the one passing over (metaphoitonta) from good ways (tropon agathon) to the more shameful (aischio), and crowns (stephanoi) with honours the one moving over (metachorounta) from the more shameful to the better, how is it not true to say that least of all (hekista) some have become base (phauloi) by nature (kata physin), or are moulded through him, but rather have become vessels of dishonour, because although it being open (meton) to them to choose (helesthai) to be approved (eudokimein) with God, they have been sick with (errhostekasi) a voluntary (ethelousion) inclination (rhopen) toward the base things? But (all') [continues in u09-open].
pass_b_english: “…like a potter, God moulds in whatever way he wishes, so as to make one vessel for honour and another for dishonour (Romans 9:21), how will reason not persuade anyone at all to think that whatever has come to be is in every way and wholly just as it was made? So one person has come into being for dishonour and has been allotted a nature of that kind, while another has been made, or rather raised up, hard, so that, as he himself says, his name may be proclaimed in all the earth (Exodus 9:16; Romans 9:17). What charge, then, can still be brought against those who fall? For they were made for this.”

To such arguments one might reply, first of all, that they could not claim that the force of these thoughts hints to us at differences of nature. For he did not say that some were made harsh and hardened, or made into vessels of honour and of dishonour, nor did he assign them such a nature at all. Rather, he leads us to think this: that some are moulded like vessels of clay, some for honour and some for dishonour; and we have been taught the meaning of the illustration from the words of the prophets. In what way, then, some are moulded as if by a potter, some for honour and others for dishonour, and for what causes, anyone may learn by reading the words of Jeremiah. It is written thus:

“Arise and go down to the potter’s house, and there you will hear my words. And I went down to the potter’s house, and there he was, making a piece of work on the stones. And the vessel that he was making fell in his hands; and again he made it into another vessel, as it seemed good in his sight to make it. And the word of the Lord came,” he says, “to me, saying: Shall I not be able to make you as this potter does, house of Israel? Look, like the potter’s clay, you are in my hands. At last I will speak against a nation or against a kingdom, to root them out; and that nation will turn from all its evils, and I will relent concerning the evils that I planned to do to them. And at last I will speak concerning a nation and concerning a kingdom, to build it up and to plant it; and they will do evil before me, so as not to hear my voice, and I will relent concerning the good things that I said I would do for them” (Jeremiah 18:2–10).

Do you see how some are moulded for honour and for dishonour, not because they were allotted a nature made that way, but because they receive an equal and fitting return for what they do? So if the Maker of all punishes the one who passes from good ways to more shameful ones, and crowns with honours the one who moves from the more shameful to the better, how is it not true to say that some have by no means become evil by nature, or been moulded so by him, but have rather become vessels of dishonour because, though it was open to them to choose to win approval with God, they fell sick with a willing inclination toward evil? But…

review_notes: Staged row fixed in tr8.json. The objection's closing quotation mark had no opening mark in this row (u08-rem-mid closes its own “If…”), so the row now opens “…. Jeremiah 18:6 LXX τοῦ ποιῆσαι ὑμᾶς is 'make you', which carries Cyril's moulding argument; 'deal with you' lost it. Cyril's inserted φησί ('he says') in 18:5 was omitted; restored. Archaic 'behold' (twice) replaced with plain English.
Copy-text: PG 74; Fragmenta in Romanos via Khazarzar (Fragmenta in sancti Pauli epistulam ad Romanos.pdf).

Section opens mid-sentence: u08-rem-mid ends with the objection's first word Εἰ ('If…'), opened there with a quotation mark; this row continues the objection with a leading ellipsis and closes the quotation at γεγόνασι γὰρ εἰς τοῦτο ('For they were made for this').
ἁπαστισοῦν: run-together form in the edition, read as ἅπαντα τινὰ οὖν / ἁπαντασοῦν, 'anyone at all'.

ἡ γραφή in ποία… ἔτι τοῖς πταίουσιν ἡ γραφή is the legal sense 'indictment, charge', not 'Scripture'; rendered 'What charge… can still be brought'. The same sense is kept for γραφῆς… τῆς ἐν νόμῳ in u09-rem-mid.
διαπλάττω / πλάττομαι: 'mould', matching 'moulded by the potter’s hand' in u08-rem-mid.
μετανοήσω (LXX, of God): rendered 'I will relent', the standard sense when God is the subject; literally 'I will repent'.
ἐπὶ τῶν λίθων (LXX): 'on the stones', kept as Cyril quotes it (the potter's wheel); πέρας (LXX): 'at last'.

ἐθελούσιον ἠῤῥωστήκασι τὴν εἰς τὰ φαῦλα ῥοπήν: accusative of respect, 'they fell sick with a willing inclination toward evil'. Cyril's point is that the inclination is chosen (ἐθελούσιον), not given by nature.
Page numbers 230 and 231 and the footer numeral '24' are edition apparatus and are omitted.
Section ends at Ἀλλ' ('But…'); the objection continues at the start of u09-open (ἐσκλήρυνεν αὐτὸς, φησὶ…).
